HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded answer)

In the hundred-year-slice PCA on the 12 forms of capital, the three symbolic-capital components — house size (Zhausgr), daggers (ZDolch) and hatchets/swords (ZAxtSchwert) — form a coherent, tightly clustered block on PC1: all three load POSITIVELY with moderate, nearly equal magnitude (hatchet/sword +0.299, dagger +0.266, house size +0.225; range 0.074, variance 0.0014). They move together as a 'symbolic capital' group that co-varies with the top-ranked PC1 variables (copper/gold +0.407, pottery decoration +0.382, depot +0.340) rather than defining the axis on their own. Along PC2 the group fans out: hatchet/sword (+0.054) and dagger (+0.074) load near zero and stay tightly paired (Δ=0.020), while house size loads distinctly higher (+0.327), making it the outlier of the trio (PC2 range 0.273, variance 0.0232). So: unified, moderate positive PC1 values for all three; on PC2 the weapons (hatchet/sword, dagger) are essentially neutral and house size stands apart, carrying the symbolic group's PC2 expression. PC1 explains 30.3% and PC2 19.5% of variance (4 components exceed Kaiser's criterion). Temporally, PC1 scores peak in the later slices (c. 1400–1000 BCE), consistent with the symbolic variables' own peaks (hatchet/sword c. 1600–1300 BCE, daggers c. 2100–1400 BCE, house size c. 3500–3400 and 1100 BCE).

payload.hypothesis: In the hundred-year-slice PCA on forms of capital, the symbolic-capital variables — hatchet/sword (PC1 +0.299, PC2 +0.054), dagger (PC1 +0.266, PC2 +0.074) and house size (PC1 +0.225, PC2 +0.327) — load positively with tight, moderate, near-equal values on PC1 (range 0.074), forming a coherent symbolic-capital block that co-varies with, but does not dominate, the axis (top PC1 loadings: copper/gold +0.407, pottery decoration +0.382, depot +0.340). Across PC2 the group fans out: hatchet/sword and dagger load near zero and stay paired (Δ 0.020), while house size loads distinctly higher (+0.327; trio PC2 range 0.273), making house size the outlier carrying the group's PC2 expression. PC1 explains 30.3% and PC2 19.5% of variance; PC1 scores peak in later slices (c. 1400-1000 BCE).
payload.workflow: SVD PCA (correlation matrix, center+scale) on the 12 Z-columns of capital.csv (39 x 100-yr slices, BCE 4300-500; 0 missing values) with svd_flip sign convention (largest-abs-loading positive per component); note ZSichel has below-unit std (0.54) so standardization was applied uniformly; loadings read from V^T, scores = Xs @ V[:2]^T.
